title: 66. Numeracy & Number Systems: Divisibility Rules for Small Integers
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a number divisible by 3 using the digit-sum rule.
questions.question: Which number is divisible by \(3\)?
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by \(3\) if the sum of its digits is a multiple of \(3\). For \(123\), the digit sum is \(1+2+3=6\), which is divisible by \(3\). For \(124\), the digit sum is \(1+2+4=7\), which is not divisible by \(3\). Therefore, \(123\) is divisible by \(3\).
questions.hint: Add the digits and check whether the sum is a multiple of \(3\).

questions.learningObjective: Identify a number divisible by 9 using the digit-sum rule.
questions.question: Which number is divisible by \(9\)?
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by \(9\) if the sum of its digits is a multiple of \(9\). For \(738\), the digit sum is \(7+3+8=18\), which is divisible by \(9\). For \(739\), the digit sum is \(7+3+9=19\), which is not divisible by \(9\). Therefore, \(738\) is divisible by \(9\).
questions.hint: Add the digits and check whether the sum is a multiple of \(9\).

questions.learningObjective: Identify a number divisible by 4 using the last-two-digits rule.
questions.question: Which number is divisible by \(4\)?
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by \(4\) if the number formed by its last two digits is divisible by \(4\). For \(1{,}234\), the last two digits are \(34\), and \(34\) is not divisible by \(4\). For \(1{,}236\), the last two digits are \(36\), and \(36\) is divisible by \(4\). Therefore, \(1{,}236\) is divisible by \(4\).
questions.hint: Check only the number formed by the last two digits.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a number divisible by 6 using divisibility by 2 and 3.
questions.question: Which number is divisible by \(6\)?
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by \(6\) if it is divisible by both \(2\) and \(3\). The number \(321\) is odd, so it is not divisible by \(2\). The number \(414\) is even, so it is divisible by \(2\), and its digit sum is \(4+1+4=9\), so it is divisible by \(3\). Therefore, \(414\) is divisible by \(6\).
questions.hint: Check whether the number is even and whether its digit sum is a multiple of \(3\).

questions.learningObjective: Identify a number divisible by 8 using the last-three-digits rule.
questions.question: Which number is divisible by \(8\)?
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by \(8\) if the number formed by its last three digits is divisible by \(8\). For \(5{,}312\), the last three digits are \(312\), and \(312 \div 8 = 39\), so \(312\) is divisible by \(8\). For \(5{,}314\), the last three digits are \(314\), which is not divisible by \(8\). Therefore, \(5{,}312\) is divisible by \(8\).
questions.hint: Check the number formed by the last three digits.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a number divisible by 5 using the last-digit rule.
questions.question: Which number is divisible by \(5\)?
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by \(5\) if its units digit is \(0\) or \(5\). The number \(2{,}342\) ends in \(2\), so it is not divisible by \(5\). The number \(2{,}345\) ends in \(5\), so it is divisible by \(5\). Therefore, \(2{,}345\) is divisible by \(5\).
questions.hint: Look at the units digit of each number.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a number divisible by 10 using the last-digit rule.
questions.question: Which number is divisible by \(10\)?
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by \(10\) if its units digit is \(0\). The number \(4{,}505\) ends in \(5\), so it is not divisible by \(10\). The number \(4{,}500\) ends in \(0\), so it is divisible by \(10\). Therefore, \(4{,}500\) is divisible by \(10\).
questions.hint: A number divisible by \(10\) must end in \(0\).

questions.learningObjective: Identify a number divisible by 2 using the last-digit rule.
questions.question: Which number is divisible by \(2\)?
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by \(2\) if its units digit is even. The number \(4{,}578\) ends in \(8\), which is even, so it is divisible by \(2\). The number \(4{,}579\) ends in \(9\), which is odd, so it is not divisible by \(2\). Therefore, \(4{,}578\) is divisible by \(2\).
questions.hint: Check whether the units digit is even.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a number divisible by both 4 and 9.
questions.question: Which number is divisible by both \(4\) and \(9\)?
questions.explanation: For \(234\), the last two digits are \(34\), which is not divisible by \(4\), so \(234\) is not divisible by \(4\). For \(432\), the last two digits are \(32\), and \(32\) is divisible by \(4\). Also, the digit sum of \(432\) is \(4+3+2=9\), so it is divisible by \(9\). Therefore, \(432\) is divisible by both \(4\) and \(9\).
questions.hint: Check divisibility by \(4\) and by \(9\) separately.

questions.concept: Finding a Missing Digit Using Divisibility by 3
questions.learningObjective: Determine a missing digit that makes a four-digit number divisible by 3.
questions.question: The four-digit number \(3\Box 52\) is divisible by \(3\). Which digit can replace the blank?
questions.explanation: Let the missing digit be \(x\). The digit sum is \(3+x+5+2=10+x\). For the number to be divisible by \(3\), \(10+x\) must be a multiple of \(3\). If \(x=5\), then \(10+5=15\), which is divisible by \(3\). If \(x=7\), then \(10+7=17\), which is not divisible by \(3\). Among the displayed options, only \(5\) works. All valid digits are \(2\), \(5\), \(8\), since the digit sum must be divisible by \(3\).
questions.hint: Let the missing digit be \(x\), then use the digit-sum rule for divisibility by \(3\).
